newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Chevron sees Australia Gorgon deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Chevron sees Australia Gorgon deal.

text.p: Chevron Corp said on Thursday it is confident an agreement will be reached to develop the giant Gorgon gas field off the coast of Western Australia.

John Powell, general manager of coordination for the Gorgon project for Chevron's wholly-owned subsidiary, Chevron Asiatic Ltd, told Reuters negotiations were progressing with the North West Shelf Project partnership to include Gorgon in its proposed expansion of liquified natural gas (LNG) production.
A combined expansion of the North West Shelf and development of Gorgon would represent Australia's largest resources project ever, costing about A$10 billion to fully develop, he said.
Some $A200 million would be generated annually for at least 20 years from a joint development, mainly through sales of LNG to Japan, Powell said.
"Chevron has come to the conclusion that the optimal way to develop Gorgon is in a cooperative manner," Powell said.
Talks centre on future ownership of the Chrysaor gas zone adjacent to Gorgon, which is owned 50-50 by Chevron and Texaco but would be part of the Gorgon development plan, he said.
Chevron, Texaco and Shell each hold two-seventh stakes in Gorgon, with Mobil owning one-seventh, all under the umbrealla group West Australian Pty Ltd (WAPET) joint venture.
Equal one-sixth partners in the North West Shelf project are Chevron, Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd, Royal/Dutch Shell, British Petroleum, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) and Woodside, the operator.
Powell said Gorgon is capable of producing between 12 million and 15 million tonnes of LNG annually for 20 years.
The North West shelf currently produces about 7.3 million tonnes of LMG a year and has proposed its own expansion to some 14 million tonnes annually.
Woodside told Reuters the North West Shelf partners would "welcome" Gorgon, provided it could "add value" to LNG expansion plans.
